title: Flat K-flat lifts of resolved global Hom evaluations
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use a small representative of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_X$ for localization and $\underline U_X$ for the termwise constant realization of an $A$-complex $U$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf, def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Tensor complexes use the direct-sum total convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $E$ be a bounded complex of flat module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $C=R\Gamma(X,R\mathcal Hom_A(E,K))\in D(A)$, with internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the constant/sections derived adjunction [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism].

There exists a K-injective representative $I$ of $K$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The global Hom complex $C_E=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I)$, with differential $df=d_If-(-1)^{|f|}fd_E$ [def-pur-hom-complex], canonically represents $C$ as an object of $D(A)$. There exists a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:U\to C_E$ with $U$ K-flat and termwise flat [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every such $I,U,\alpha$, the formula
$$t:\underline U_X\otimes_A E\longrightarrow I,\qquad t(w\otimes e)=\alpha(w)(e)$$
defines a chain map. Its source is K-flat with flat terms, and its localization is the derived evaluation $\underline C_X\otimes_A^LE\to K$ obtained from the derived constant/sections counit and internal evaluation. There exist chain maps
$$\underline U_X\otimes_A E\xrightarrow{u}N\xrightarrow{c}I$$
with $N$ K-flat with flat terms, $c$ a quasi-isomorphism, and $cu$ chain homotopic to $t$. Under the canonical source and target identifications, $Q_X(c)Q_X(u)=Q_X(t)$. Moreover, for every scheme morphism $f:Z\to X$, exact constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] preserves the K-flat flat-term complexes $\underline U_X$, $E$, $\underline U_X\otimes_A E$ and $N$, and their ordinary pullbacks compute their derived pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat), with sections Hom complexes and Internal hom in the derived category; agent refinement for global evaluation, constant realization and flat sources, from old proof steps 1 and 3 of lem-pur-external-rhom-cone-pairing.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $K$ and apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the stipulated small etale site to obtain a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex $I$. The same theorem applies to any complex, so the bounded-below hypothesis presents no restriction. Since $E$ is bounded and termwise flat, it is bounded above and hence K-flat by clause (1) of [lem-kun-kflat-criteria].

For any K-injective representative $I$ of $K$, put $H=\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(E,I)$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $Q_X(H)$ canonically represents $R\mathcal Hom_A(E,K)$; this definition explicitly permits any K-injective target representative. Because $E$ is K-flat, [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] says that $H$ is K-injective. Thus [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] computes $C$ by $\Gamma(X,H)$, retaining its $A$-module structure in each degree: the identity of $H$ is a K-injective resolution of the representative $H$, and [lem-kun-rgamma-unbounded-well-defined] says that the object so obtained is canonically isomorphic to the one from any other representative, resolution and comparison. The degreewise equivalences and differential equation of [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-cochains] identify this complex with $C_E^n=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_X(E^p,I^{p+n})$, with $d(f)=d_If-(-1)^nfd_E$. All identifications here are $A$-linear: sections and the component projections are $A$-linear, and the degreewise maps send a section to its family of $A_X$-module maps. This proves the asserted representation in $D(A)$, rather than only an identification of its cohomology groups.

Regard $A$-modules as sheaves on the one-object site with only the identity arrow and its trivial topology. Applying [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] there to $C_E$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:U\to C_E$ with $U$ K-flat and all $U^n$ flat. This is an ordinary $A$-complex: sheaves on this site are exactly $A$-modules, and its total tensor is the module total tensor. For every such choice, [lem-sfb-constant-module-kflat] gives K-flatness of $\underline U_X$, and [lem-sfb-constant-module-flat] gives flatness of every term. The exact realization of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] identifies $Q_X(\underline U_X)$ with $\underline C_X$ through the isomorphism induced by $\alpha$.

Use the identification $C_E=\Gamma(X,H)$ from step 2. The ordinary constant/sections adjunction underlying [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], applied termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], sends $\alpha:U\to\Gamma(X,H)$ to the chain map $\beta:\underline U_X\to H$. Explicitly, $\beta$ is the composite $\underline U_X\xrightarrow{\underline\alpha}\underline{\Gamma(X,H)}_X\to H$, with the ordinary counit as last arrow. For $w\in U^n$, its image is the section of $H^n$ corresponding to the family $\alpha(w)^p:E^p\to I^{p+n}$. This description uses the differential-compatible equivalences of [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-cochains].

Define $t$ on each tensor summand of bidegree $(n,p)$ by $w\otimes e\mapsto\alpha(w)^p(e)$, using $\beta$ from step 4. This is balanced and $A$-bilinear, hence gives a map from the sheaf tensor product; it commutes with restrictions since each component of $\beta$ is a sheaf-Hom section. Locally a constant section $w$ is represented by an element of $U^n$, so this formula determines the sheaf map, and the total direct sum determines a graded map. Using [def-pur-hom-complex] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], its chain equation is the following calculation for homogeneous $w,e$:
$$d_I\bigl(\alpha(w)(e)\bigr)=(d_{C_E}\alpha(w))(e)+(-1)^n\alpha(w)(d_Ee)=\alpha(d_Uw)(e)+(-1)^n\alpha(w)(d_Ee)=t\bigl(d_Uw\otimes e+(-1)^nw\otimes d_Ee\bigr).$$
The two mixed signs agree also for negative $n$; no factor is interchanged, so no additional Koszul sign occurs.

source.place: Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), signed differential and total tensor-Hom calculation 0A90 (lemma-compose).

proof.text: Both $\underline U_X$ and $E$ are K-flat and have flat terms by steps 1 and 3. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] to them. It gives that $D=\operatorname{Tot}(\underline U_X\otimes_A E)$ is K-flat, that each $D^r=\bigoplus_{n+p=r}\underline{U^n}_X\otimes_A E^p$ is flat, and that $Q_X(D)$ canonically computes $\underline C_X\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E$ under step 3's identification. Thus the actual source of $t$ is a valid derived tensor representative.

source.place: Tag 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat) and Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); flat tensor terms in Modules on Sites 0G6Q (lemma-tensor-flats).

proof.text:
The derived constant/sections adjunction is the induced adjunction specified by [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] with $G$ the constant-module functor and $F=\Gamma(X,-)$. Constants are additive and exact by [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], so all homotopy complexes form a left resolving class on which $G$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The target module-sheaf category has unbounded K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply the normalized formula to $\beta:\underline U_X\to H$, whose target is K-injective by step 2. Its ordinary transpose is $\alpha$. The adjunction of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] is the one with this normalization: every object of $D(A)$ is $Q_A(M)$ for a complex $M$ and every object of $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is $Q_X$ of a K-injective complex, and morphisms $Q_X(\underline M_X)\to Q_X(J)$ with $J$ K-injective are homotopy classes of chain maps $\underline M_X\to J$, so the displayed formula fixes the adjunction bijection on all pairs of objects. Therefore, under $Q_A(C_E)\cong R\Gamma(X,Q_XH)$, the derived transpose of $Q_X(\beta)$ is $Q_A(\alpha)$. Equivalently,
$$Q_X(\beta)=\varepsilon_{Q_XH}\circ\underline{Q_A(\alpha)}_X.$$
Here the derived-unit comparison at $H$ is the canonical sections identification from step 2. Since $Q_A(\alpha)$ is the chosen isomorphism $Q_AU\cong C$, this identifies $Q_X(\beta)$ with the derived constant/sections counit at $R\mathcal Hom_A(E,K)$.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), normalized ordinary transpose; Cohomology on Sites 07A6 (lemma-adjoint).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] with its $P=E$, its K-injective target equal to $I$, its arbitrary first complex equal to $\underline U_X$, and its chain map equal to $\beta$. The hypotheses are step 1's K-flat flat-term assertion for $E$ and the stipulated K-injectivity of $I$. The lemma says that the derived tensor-Hom transpose of $Q_X(\beta)$ is represented by $w\otimes e\mapsto\beta(w)(e)$, exactly the map $t$ of step 5, with factor order $\underline U_X,E$. Combining this with step 7 yields
$$Q_X(t)=\operatorname{ev}_{E,K}\circ(\varepsilon_{R\mathcal Hom_A(E,K)}\otimes 1_E)$$
under $Q_AU\cong C$, the constant-realization identification, and $Q_XI\cong K$. This is precisely the derived evaluation asserted in the item. The argument applies to every allowed $I,U,\alpha$, since both cited representative formulas do.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), proof with arbitrary first complex, K-flat second complex and K-injective target.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kflat-map-factorization] to the chain map $t:D\to I$. Step 6 verifies both required conditions on $D$: K-flatness and flatness of all terms. We obtain $D\xrightarrow{u}N\xrightarrow{c}I$, with $N$ K-flat with flat terms, $c$ a quasi-isomorphism, and a chain homotopy $t\simeq cu$. The localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] factors through the homotopy category, so the homotopic maps have equal images. Functoriality gives $Q_X(c)Q_X(u)=Q_X(cu)=Q_X(t)$, with the same source and target identifications as in step 8.

source.place: Tag 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat), including its final flat-terms clause; derived localization through the homotopy category (Derived Categories 05RR).

proof.text: Let $f:Z\to X$ be any scheme morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures](1), $f^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets is left adjoint to $f_*$ and commutes with finite limits, so $(f^{-1},f_*)$ is a morphism of topoi $\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $f^{-1}A_X\cong A_Z$, the module inverse image is the ringed-topos pullback $f^{-1}(-)\otimes_{f^{-1}A_X}A_Z$ for this ring identification, and it is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] separately to $\underline U_X$, $E$, $D$ and $N$: all four are K-flat with flat terms by steps 1, 3, 6 and 9. Their ordinary pullbacks are consequently K-flat with flat terms. Exactness shows that termwise $f^{-1}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms: it preserves kernels, images and cokernels, hence cohomology and its isomorphisms. It therefore descends directly to the localization. This descended functor computes its left derived functor, with the identity representative comparison, since every complex is adapted to an exact functor. In particular the four ordinary pullbacks compute the stated derived pullbacks, without any flatness or smoothness assumption on the scheme morphism.
